releases.displayName: Second Stability Update for Transport Fever 3 Released

items.text: We are happy to release the second stability and performance update for Transport Fever 3 today. A big thank you to all who had participated in testing on the preview branch and given us feedback during the past weeks. We plan to continue supporting the game for a long time, and it is feedback like this that helps us to understand where we can make the biggest difference.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45628540/3acf536d11b1e59e5b72191c0f73a6db188bd0a8.jpg"]

The first update released to players on PC, Mac and Linux has definitely improved performance for many players, and some of the stability problems we have seen reported have either been eliminated entirely or at least reduced. The update for players on PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series X|S is currently in testing and will be released in the near future.

We won't be satisfied until the game performs smoothly for as many players as possible, which is why we are working on further updates that are focused on this side of the game. We hope that our newly released second performance update will help more players remove problems from their game - and this won't be the last.
You can find the full release notes here.
If you are experiencing additional issues, that are not addressed with this patch, please share them with us using our offical forum.

One of the challenges we have encountered is that mods can make it difficult to determine whether an issue is caused by the game itself or by a mod. Fortunately, the game's built-in automatic logging helps us identify where players are experiencing problems and, when necessary, work with mod authors to resolve conflicts as quickly as possible. At the same time, we are putting more effort into improving the mod hub, focusing on both stability to make browsing mods more reliable and user interface improvements that will bring some of the functionality you have been asking for.

We're also well under way on our first gameplay update which will remove anachronistic building designs and make the first improvements to the user interface to help you connect with your game world better.

Since completing testing for this update we became aware of a conflict that affects Nvidia graphics card users with the freshly released 621.01 GeForce drivers. We have a fix for this conflict in testing, but rather than delay this update to include it, we have opted to complete the testing process first. This fix is already available on the public preview branch. For the time being we recommend that Nvidia graphics card users do not update their drivers or, if they have done so already, roll back to a previous driver version. Once testing is complete, we will release a hotfix to support the new drivers.

Thank you again for playing the game and for taking the time to share your feedback. It's wonderful to see so many of you enjoying Transport Fever 3, and your feedback is invaluable in helping us understand where we can make further improvements.
The Urban Games Team

releases.displayName: Transport Fever 3 Receives First Stability Update

items.text: The first week after the release of Transport Fever 3 has been an exciting one for the team at Urban Games. Years of work finally being experienced and enjoyed by players is something we have been looking forward to.

As part of the release of the game we have listened to and read the feedback from a great many players around the world. While we are delighted by the tremendous interest in the game and all the positive feedback we have received, we are particularly paying attention to those who are not finding the game as enjoyable as we expected and hoped it would be. We have read your reviews and comments and we believe we understand the main causes for any disappointment, so it is the highest priority for us that we address these concerns quickly.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45628540/c9cd4225ed3114aefbe9b5b62a553f17b2f7c1e3.jpg"]

The first thing that we are aiming to do is ensure that the game runs smoothly without any problems for as many people as possible. We have released our first stability update today which should improve a good number of stability and performance issues, and we will review feedback from this update to make further improvements.
Please find the release notes here.
This stability update does not address every issue, if your particular issue has not been fixed yet, please rest assured that we are doing everything we can to resolve it in future stability updates.

We have listened to your comments regarding the user interface and in particular the number of clicks some actions require, and will be simplifying as many of these functions as we can without losing functionality. We have also heard to your comments regarding the quality of localisation for the game and are working to eliminate confusing or inadequate text as quickly as possible. And yes, we have also seen the critisism regarding anachronistic content in the game, and we will address this as well.

One of the more regular areas of concern is with regard to the mod hub and we are actively investigating this for improvement. Modding is a critical part of making the game feel personal to your own goals, so improving the mod hub is something we'll look at constantly over the life of the game.

While this update addresses issues specific to players on PC, Mac and Linux on Steam, and will also be rolled out to players on GOG and EGS in the coming days, there will be future updates for players on PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series X|S. Our goal with the game is to continue to improve it over time, and it is thanks to your feedback that we understand where that improvement is most needed. Thank you for caring enough to explain where the game is not performing as you would expect, and we will be ensuring a great experience for all players as quickly as possible.
The Urban Games Team
